#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --job-name=job_wgpu
#   --open-mode=append
#   --output=./%j_%x.out
#   --error=./%j_%x.err
#   --export=ALL
#   --time=00:10:00
#   --gres=gpu:1
#   --mem=64G
#   -c 4

#flux: --job-name=job_wgpu
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 4
#flux: --time-limit=10m

# Omitted Slurm option: --gres=gpu:1
# Flux GPU requests are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without a GPU, causing failure or severe slowdown.

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem=64G
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm options: --output/--error with %j/%x tokens and --open-mode=append
# Slurm token expansion (%j jobid, %x jobname) and open-mode append semantics are not portable in Flux output directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide and append behavior may not be preserved.

# Omitted Slurm option: --export=ALL
# Flux does not have a portable directive identical to Slurm --export.
# Performance implication: environment differences could affect runtime behavior; export needed variables explicitly if required.

singularity exec --nv \
  --overlay "$SCRATCH/overlay-50G-10M.ext3:ro" \
  /scratch/work/public/singularity/cuda10.1-cudnn7-devel-ubuntu18.04-20201207.sif \
  /bin/bash -c "
source /ext3/env.sh
conda activate
python ./test_gpu.py
"
